children: could be positioned for a much larger opportunity inside the Federal Aviation Administration as the agency begins putting artificial intelligence into live air-traffic operations, according to Rosenblatt. Analyst John McPeake says the FAA's modernization push reinforces Palantir's role on the safety and analytics side, potentially expanding a government relationship that began with an $18 million contract in 2021.
The latest catalyst is the FAA's rollout of its AI-powered Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories system, or SMART, at the three major airports serving Washington, D.C.
The deployment marks the first live U.S. operation of the technology and is designed to help identify congestion and other airspace problems before they develop.

McPeake argues investors should not view the broader modernization effort simply as a winner-take-all contest between Palantir and Aviation Systems International. ASI won the flight-operations portion of the program through an $875 million, 12-year contract, while Palantir is positioned around safety, analytics and data integration.

That distinction could be important. Rosenblatt expects Palantir's Foundry and Artificial Intelligence Platform to combine data from siloed FAA systems and identify risks such as unsafe aircraft spacing or patterns that could provide early warnings of future incidents.

The FAA's fiscal 2027 performance plan specifically identifies Foundry as a platform for integrating safety data and applying AI and machine learning to aviation risks. McPeake therefore sees the possibility of substantially higher FAA spending in 2027, particularly around the ASKME program.

The FAA opportunity arrives as Palantir's government business is already accelerating. Government revenue grew 79% year over year in the second quarter of 2026, while commercial revenue rose 110%, including 149% growth in U.S. commercial sales.
For investors, the next proof point is whether live FAA deployments translate into larger contract awards and recurring spending.
McPeake reiterated a Buy rating and $225 price target, implying about 19% upside. The broader analyst consensus is more restrained, with an average target of $201.74 implying roughly 5% upside.

title: Rosenblatt Has Message For Palantir Stock Investors
